cohort: The study included women delivering a singleton, non-anomalous infant at >=36 weeks' gestation, comparing those diagnosed with neonatal encephalopathy (cases, n = 109) with a control group of women with unaffected infants (n = 233).
finding: Category III fetal heart rate tracings, bradycardia, minimal/absent variability, late decelerations, and prolonged decelerations were independently associated with neonatal encephalopathy, while accelerations were found to be protective.
